app.title: GPUMD Insight — Universal Trajectory Viewer
app.summary: A person loads one or two multi-frame atomistic trajectories, either bundled examples or uploaded extended XYZ files, and chooses whether to view one structure or two side by side. They pick the elements or atoms to focus on, choose between the whole periodic cell and a local environment around the focus, and set how the atoms are drawn. They then choose an element pair and a distance cutoff. They scrub or play a single shared timeline that drives both 3D viewers and a strip of per-frame measures together. Below the viewers, curves show how the minimum pair distance, the pair count and the mean coordination change over the run, so the two runs can be compared frame by frame.

task.text: Play back one or two simulated atomistic trajectories on a linked timeline and compare how pair distances and coordination around chosen atoms change over the run.

data.text: Multi-frame atomistic simulation trajectories: each frame has atom positions, element symbols, a periodic cell and a time stamp.
data.item: a frame of a simulation trajectory, with every atom's element and position in a periodic cell

stage.text: exploring and comparing simulation trajectories after a run, before quantitative analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls pick the datasets, the focus atoms, the view scope and an element-pair cutoff. These build one or two 3D viewers that share a single frame slider and play button, with a strip of per-frame measures read at the current frame. Plotted curves of the same measures across all frames mark the current frame with a vertical line.

field.text: trajectory visualisation and pair-distance and coordination analysis of molecular dynamics simulations

workflow.name: play back two runs on a shared timeline and compare per-frame measures

steps.here: Choose the bundled examples or upload one or two multi-frame extended XYZ files. Each file is checked for a constant atom count and order and a full 3D cell.

steps.step: choose one item or two to compare side by side
steps.here: Workspace mode switches between a single structure and two structures compared side by side, with primary and comparison dataset pickers.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Pick focus elements or type 1-based atom numbers. Then either show the full cell or only atoms within a local-environment radius of the focus. Hydrogen can be hidden, and the drawing style can be ball-and-stick, space-filling or framework.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For a chosen element pair and cutoff, every frame gets a minimum-image distance, a pair count and a mean coordination. An optional preset adds cluster span, the largest connected component and a second coordination.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: One slider, a play/pause button and previous/next buttons move every viewer to the same frame and show the frame number and time in picoseconds.

Two colour-bordered viewers share bounds and a frame. The metric strip shows each run's value at the current frame next to the other's. Clicking an atom labels it with its element, number and coordinates.

steps.step: look at how a measure changes over the run
steps.here: Two stacked line charts plot distance, then count and coordination, against frame for each run, with a red line at the current frame.

distinctive: Distances and bonds follow periodic boundaries (the minimum-image convention), and bonds that cross the cell edge are drawn to faded ghost images of the atoms on the other side.
The compared runs are cut to the shorter one's frame count, and one timeline uses the median time per frame, so both viewers always show the same moment.
The local-environment scope recentres each frame on the focus atoms and shows only atoms within a set radius.

Analysis is a plugin: a generic element-pair measure, plus a system-specific preset that adds cluster span and largest connected component, shown with a caution against reading the results quantitatively.
A presentation mode hides the sidebar and forces a two-run comparison for a 16:9 slide capture.
